title: Beginner Pack 6
subtitle: Time Points, Movement Extent & Polite Past Actions
label: 3 patterns · 6 questions
rationale: Extends the learner's toolkit to temporal anchors and completed events: (1) specific time particle に pins an action to a clock hour, (2) span pattern から…まで connects a starting boundary to an ending boundary across time or space, and (3) polite past endings ました / ませんでした build directly on Pack 4’s ます / ません so learners can describe completed or non-completed past actions.
description: Learn time particle に for clock hours, span pattern から…まで for spans of time and space, and polite past verbs ました / ませんでした.

patterns.readingNote: に marks the specific clock hour or point in time when an event happens.
patterns.summary: You have seen に for location (Pack 1) and destination (Pack 4). When paired with specific clock times containing numbers (一時, 三時, 七時), に marks the exact point in time when an action takes place (三時に行きます = go at 3 o'clock).

examples.japanese: 大人は三時にホテルに入ります。
examples.reading: おとなは さんじに ホテルに はいります。
examples.gloss: 大人 adult · 三時 3 o'clock · に at (time) · ホテル hotel · 入ります enter
examples.english: The adult enters the hotel at 3 o'clock.

examples.japanese: 女の人は一時に来ます。
examples.reading: おんなの ひとは いちじに きます。
examples.gloss: 女の人 woman · 一時 1 o'clock · に at (time) · 来ます come

questions.prompt: Choose the particle that marks 三時 (3 o'clock) as the specific time the adult enters the hotel:
questions.japanese: 大人は三時（　）ホテルに入ります。
questions.targetMeaning: The adult enters the hotel at 3 o'clock.
questions.reading: おとなは さんじ（　）ホテルに はいります。
questions.gloss: 大人 adult · 三時 3 o'clock · ホテル hotel · 入ります enter

choices.text: を
choices.explanation: Not quite. を marks the direct object of an action, but 三時 is a specific time marker.

choices.text: に
choices.explanation: That’s right! に marks specific points in time, such as clock hours (三時に = at 3 o'clock).

choices.text: と
choices.explanation: Not quite. と marks accompaniment (with someone) or links nouns, not a specific point in time.

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — Choose the particle that marks 一時 (1 o'clock) as the time the woman comes:
followUp.reading: おんなの ひとは いちじ（　）きます。
followUp.gloss: 女の人 woman · 一時 1 o'clock · 来ます come

choices.text: に
choices.explanation: That’s right! に attaches to numerical clock times to indicate when an event happens (一時に = at 1 o'clock).

choices.text: で
choices.explanation: Not quite. で marks the location of an activity or total duration, not a single clock time point.

choices.text: の
choices.explanation: Not quite. の connects two nouns together, not a time noun to the verb 来ます.

workedExample.japanese: 女の人は一時に来ます。
workedExample.reading: おんなの ひとは いちじに きます。
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: State the time: 一時 (“1 o'clock”). Step 2: Mark specific time with に (一時に = “at 1 o'clock”). Step 3: Complete with the action verb 来ます (“comes”).

questions.japanese: 二人は七時に駅に行きます。
questions.reading: ふたりは しちじに えきに いきます。
questions.gloss: 二人 two people · 七時 7 o'clock · に at · 駅 station · に to · 行きます go

choices.text: Seven people go to the station together.
choices.explanation: Not quite. 七人 (しちにん) is seven people, but 七時 (しちじ) means 7 o'clock; the topic is 二人は (two people).

choices.text: Two people stay at the station for seven hours.
choices.explanation: Not quite. 七時間 would mean seven hours; 七時に means “at 7 o'clock,” and 行きます is “go.”

choices.text: The two people go to the station at 7 o'clock.
choices.explanation: That’s right! 二人は is “the two people,” 七時に is “at 7 o'clock,” and 駅に行きます is “go to the station.”

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — What does this sentence mean?
followUp.japanese: あの人は八時にへやを出ます。
followUp.reading: あの ひとは はちじに へやを でます。
followUp.gloss: あの人 that person · 八時 8 o'clock · に at · へや room · 出ます leave

choices.text: Eight people enter the room together.
choices.explanation: Not quite. 八人は is eight people; 八時に is the time “at 8 o'clock,” and 出ます means “leaves,” not “enters.”

choices.text: That person leaves the room at 8 o'clock.
choices.explanation: That’s right! あの人は is “that person,” 八時に is “at 8 o'clock,” and へやを出ます is “leaves the room.”

choices.text: That person rests in the room until 8 o'clock.
choices.explanation: Not quite. 出ます means “leaves,” not “rests” (休みます), and に marks the time of departure, not “until” (まで).

workedExample.japanese: あの人は八時にへやを出ます。
workedExample.reading: あの ひとは はちじに へやを でます。
workedExample.english: That person leaves the room at 8 o'clock.
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: Identify topic: あの人は (“that person”). Step 2: Identify time marked by に: 八時に (“at 8 o'clock”). Step 3: Identify action and space left: へやを出ます (“leaves the room”).

patterns.pattern: A から B まで
patterns.gloss: from A to/until B (span pattern から…まで)
patterns.readingNote: から marks the starting point and まで marks the ending limit across time or physical distance.
patterns.summary: In Pack 5, you learned から as an origin point (駅から). When paired with まで (“until / as far as”), it frames an entire span: 一時から三時まで (from 1 to 3 o'clock) or 駅からホテルまで (from the station to the hotel).

examples.japanese: 一時から三時まで勉強します。
examples.reading: いちじから さんじまで べんきょうします。
examples.gloss: 一時 1 o'clock · から from · 三時 3 o'clock · まで until · 勉強します study

examples.japanese: 駅からホテルまで歩きます。
examples.reading: えきから ホテルまで あるきます。
examples.gloss: 駅 station · から from · ホテル hotel · まで as far as · 歩きます walk
examples.english: Walk from the station to the hotel.

questions.prompt: Choose the particle that marks 三時 (3 o'clock) as the ending limit of the study session:
questions.japanese: 一時から三時（　）勉強します。
questions.reading: いちじから さんじ（　）べんきょうします。
questions.gloss: 一時 1 o'clock · から from · 三時 3 o'clock · 勉強します study

choices.text: まで
choices.explanation: That’s right! まで marks the final endpoint or limit of a duration (三時まで = until 3 o'clock).

choices.text: から
choices.explanation: Not quite. から marks the starting point (一時から); repeating から would mean starting at 3 o'clock.

choices.text: に
choices.explanation: Not quite. に marks a single point in time, but here we are stating a continuous span ending at 3 o'clock (から…まで).

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — Choose the particle that marks ホテル (hotel) as the destination limit of the walk:
followUp.japanese: 駅からホテル（　）歩きます。
followUp.targetMeaning: Walk from the station to the hotel.
followUp.reading: えきから ホテル（　）あるきます。
followUp.gloss: 駅 station · から from · ホテル hotel · 歩きます walk

choices.text: で
choices.explanation: Not quite. で marks the area where an activity happens, not the target endpoint of a journey across distance.

choices.text: を
choices.explanation: Not quite. を marks a direct object, but 歩きます is an intransitive verb of movement.

choices.text: まで
choices.explanation: That’s right! まで marks the physical destination endpoint (ホテルまで = as far as the hotel).

workedExample.japanese: 駅からホテルまで歩きます。
workedExample.reading: えきから ホテルまで あるきます。
workedExample.english: Walk from the station to the hotel.
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: Starting point: 駅から (“from the station”). Step 2: Ending limit: ホテルまで (“to the hotel”). Step 3: Action: 歩きます (“walk”).

questions.japanese: 入り口から川まで大人二人が歩きます。
questions.reading: いりぐちから かわまで おとな ふたりが あるきます。
questions.gloss: 入り口 entrance · から from · 川 river · まで to · 大人大人 adults · 二人 two people · 歩きます walk

choices.text: Two adults enter the river through the entrance.
choices.explanation: Not quite. 川まで means “as far as / to the river,” not into it (川に入ります), and 歩きます means “walk.”

choices.text: Two adults walk from the entrance to the river.
choices.explanation: That’s right! 入り口から is “from the entrance,” 川まで is “to the river,” and 大人二人が歩きます is “two adults walk.”

choices.text: There are two adults between the entrance and the river.
choices.explanation: Not quite. This describes an active walking journey with 歩きます, not static location.

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — What does this sentence mean?
followUp.japanese: 九時から十時までへやで休みます。
followUp.reading: くじから じゅうじまで へやで やすみます。
followUp.gloss: 九時 9 o'clock · から from · 十時 10 o'clock · まで until · へや room · で in · 休みます rest

choices.text: Rest in the room from 9 o'clock until 10 o'clock.
choices.explanation: That’s right! 九時から is “from 9 o'clock,” 十時まで is “until 10 o'clock,” へやで is “in the room,” and 休みます is “rest.”

choices.text: Ten people leave the room at 9 o'clock.
choices.explanation: Not quite. 九時 and 十時 are clock hours, not numbers of people, and 休みます is “rest,” not “leave.”

choices.text: The room is open from 9 o'clock to 10 o'clock.
choices.explanation: Not quite. 休みます is “rest,” describing a person taking a break, not a room schedule.

workedExample.japanese: 九時から十時までへやで休みます。
workedExample.reading: くじから じゅうじまで へやで やすみます。
workedExample.english: Rest in the room from 9 o'clock until 10 o'clock.
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: Time span: 九時から (“from 9”) + 十時まで (“until 10”). Step 2: Location of action: へやで (“in the room”). Step 3: Verb: 休みます (“rest”).

patterns.gloss: did / did not (polite past verb endings)
patterns.readingNote: 〜ました marks polite completed past action; 〜ませんでした marks polite past negative.
patterns.summary: In Pack 4, you used polite present verbs (入ります = enter, 入りません = does not enter). Changing 〜ます to 〜ました forms the polite past affirmative (“entered / did”), and changing to 〜ませんでした forms the polite past negative (“did not enter / did not do”).

examples.japanese: きのう、あの人はビルに入りました。
examples.reading: きのう、あの ひとは ビルに はいりました。
examples.gloss: きのう yesterday · あの人 that person · ビル building · 入りました entered
examples.english: Yesterday, that person entered the building.

examples.japanese: 大人は手を上げませんでした。
examples.reading: おとなは てを あげませんでした。
examples.gloss: 大人 adult · 手 hand · を object · 上げませんでした did not raise/lift
examples.english: The adult did not raise their hand.

questions.prompt: Choose the verb form that completes “Yesterday, that person entered the building” (completed past):
questions.japanese: きのう、あの人はビルに入り（　）。
questions.targetMeaning: Yesterday, that person entered the building.
questions.reading: きのう、あの ひとは ビルに はいり（　）。
questions.gloss: きのう yesterday · あの人 that person · ビル building

choices.text: ます
choices.explanation: Not quite. ます is the present/future tense (“enters / will enter”), but きのう indicates a completed past event.

choices.text: ません
choices.explanation: Not quite. ません is present negative (“does not enter”), not affirmative past.

choices.text: ました
choices.explanation: That’s right! ました marks the completed polite past affirmative (入りました = “entered”).

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — Choose the verb form that completes “The adult did NOT raise their hand” (polite past negative):
followUp.targetMeaning: The adult did not raise their hand.
followUp.reading: おとなは てを あげ（　）。
followUp.gloss: 大人 adult · 手 hand · を object

choices.text: ました
choices.explanation: Not quite. ました is positive past (“raised / lifted”), but we need the negative “did not raise.”

choices.text: ませんでした
choices.explanation: That’s right! ませんでした is the polite past negative ending (上げませんでした = “did not raise”).

choices.text: ます
choices.explanation: Not quite. ます is present positive (“raises”), not past negative.

workedExample.japanese: 大人は手を上げませんでした。
workedExample.reading: おとなは てを あげませんでした。
workedExample.english: The adult did not raise their hand.
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: Start with verb stem: 上げ (age). Step 2: Attach polite past negative: 〜ませんでした → 上げませんでした (“did not raise”).

questions.japanese: 女の人は大きい箱を下げませんでした。
questions.reading: おんなの ひとは おおきい はこを さげませんでした。
questions.gloss: 女の人 woman · 大きい箱 big box · 下げませんでした did not lower

choices.text: The woman did not lower the big box.
choices.explanation: That’s right! 女の人は is “the woman,” 大きい箱を is “the big box,” and 下げませんでした is the polite past negative “did not lower.”

choices.text: The woman will lower the big box now.
choices.explanation: Not quite. 下げません would be present negative and 下げます present affirmative; 下げませんでした is past negative (“did not lower”).

choices.text: The woman lifted the big box yesterday.
choices.explanation: Not quite. “Lifted” is 上げました; 下げませんでした means “did not lower.”

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — What does this sentence mean?
followUp.japanese: 二人は川に入りました。
followUp.reading: ふたりは かわに はいりました。
followUp.gloss: 二人 two people · 川 river · に into · 入りました entered/went into

choices.text: Two people do not go into the river.
choices.explanation: Not quite. 入りません is present negative; 入りました is affirmative past (“went into”).

choices.text: There are two people by the river.
choices.explanation: Not quite. This is a completed action sentence with 入りました (“entered”), not an existence sentence.

choices.text: The two people went into the river.
choices.explanation: That’s right! 二人は is “the two people,” 川に is “into the river,” and 入りました is the polite past “went into / entered.”

workedExample.japanese: 二人は川に入りました。
workedExample.reading: ふたりは かわに はいりました。
workedExample.english: The two people went into the river.
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: Subject/topic: 二人は (“the two people”). Step 2: Destination: 川に (“into the river”). Step 3: Polite past verb: 入りました (“entered / went into”).

sources: Komorebi Level 1 curriculum (data/level-1.json): kanji 一, 二, 三, 七, 八, 入, 上, 下, 口, 人, 女, 川 and vocabulary 一, 二, 三, 七, 八, 入る, 上げる, 下げる, 入り口, 人, 女, 川, ふじ山.
